Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 08/21/2026
Patient: Edmond Corwin, 78-year-old male

Subjective:
Mr. Corwin presents for his routine follow-up visit. He reports no new complaints today and feels generally well. There are no specific concerns or symptoms he wishes to address.

Objective:
Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. Cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, and neurological exams are unremarkable.

Assessment:
Stable health status in an elderly male with no acute issues.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage healthy lifestyle and regular exercise. Follow-up visit scheduled in 6 months or sooner if any concerns arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/20/2026
Patient: Edmond Corwin, 78-year-old male

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/20/2026: acute osteoporotic L1 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L1 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No additional acute abnormalities are identified.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician based on clinical presentation.

notes.author: Interventional radiologist
notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/29/2026
Patient: Edmond Corwin, 78-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 08/12/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 7 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 7/10 despite 6 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and tramadol, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Clinical Findings:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Management:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program.

Plan:
Continue current pain management and bracing. Monitor symptoms closely. Consider interventional options if pain persists or worsens.
